_comment: Guided tour of the native MMFDB Admin. Every step points at a real emtk control ('name' is its rectangle in the app: an item of gui/app.py or a field / action / table of a view spec); steps with 'await' wait until the user has used that control.

steps.title: Where the database is
steps.text: The toolbar names the MMFDB server (Host and Port), the User and a Password. The dot says whether you are connected: green connected, yellow connecting, red not. A session this ChiSurf already holds is reused, so you usually need no password.

steps.title: Administrators only
steps.text: MMFDB Admin is for MMFDB administrators. Signed in as anyone else, the panels stay empty and the status bar says why. Logout drops the session; ... opens the login dialog with the server settings under Advanced.

steps.title: Pick a table
steps.text: The rail lists the panels, grouped as the database is. Open Samples.

steps.title: Its records
steps.text: One row per sample. Click a header to sort, type in the filter box to keep matching rows, right-click a header to choose columns. Pick a row: its fields open in the form below.

await.hint: Click a row of the table.

steps.title: Edit in place
steps.text: The form's fields come from the mmCIF dictionary; a field's tooltip is its definition. An edit is saved when you commit the field: press Enter or click elsewhere. There is no Save button to forget.

steps.title: Linked records
steps.text: An <u>underlined</u> cell names another record, such as a sample's project or an experiment's setup. Double-click it to open that record in its own panel.

steps.title: New and Delete
steps.text: New creates a record at once (an untitled id you then rename) and opens it. Delete deletes the ticked rows after asking.

steps.title: Where data came from
steps.text: Open Raw Data: the measured files the database knows.

steps.title: Trace it
steps.text: Pick a row, then press Use as provenance seed: the Provenance Graph opens on it and loads everything it fed into.

await.hint: Pick a row, then press Use as provenance seed.

steps.title: The provenance graph
steps.text: Inputs on the left, products on the right; click a node to read its record. Load upstream / downstream narrow the trace, Export JSON / ZIP write it out.

steps.title: More help
steps.text: Help explains every panel, the per-table actions, the workflow panels and the menus.
